acs.text: The `/publish` page lists exactly four publishing packages.

Every package card on `/publish` matches one of the specified package name, price, and turnaround combinations: Starter ($499, 45-day turnaround), Standard ($999, 30-day), Premium ($1999, 21-day), or Author's Choice ($3499, 14-day).

expected_answer.operand: package card matches one of the specified name, price, and turnaround tuples: Starter ($499, 45-day turnaround), Standard ($999, 30-day), Premium ($1999, 21-day), Author's Choice ($3499, 14-day)

acs.text: Seat availability is shared globally across visitors for the current month until a claimed seat is withdrawn or the app restarts.

expected_answer.operand: a seat claimed by any visitor is unavailable to every visitor until it is withdrawn or the app restarts

acs.text: The monthly package seat pools are capped at 6 Starter seats, 4 Standard seats, 2 Premium seats, and 1 Author's Choice seat.

expected_answer.operand: Starter 6 seats; Standard 4 seats; Premium 2 seats; Author's Choice 1 seat

acs.text: Each package card with seats remaining shows the availability message `<n> seats left this month`.

expected_answer.operand: package with seats left shows `<n> seats left this month`

acs.text: A package with exactly one remaining seat shows the singular availability message `1 seat left this month`.
Each package card with seats remaining offers `Choose <package name>`.

expected_answer.operand: package with seats left offers `Choose <package name>`

acs.text: Each fully booked package card shows `Fully booked this month`.

expected_answer.operand: package with no seats left shows `Fully booked this month`

acs.text: Each fully booked package card offers `View details`.

expected_answer.operand: package with no seats left offers `View details`

acs.text: No fully booked package card offers `Choose <package name>`.

expected_answer.operand: package with no seats left offers `Choose <package name>`

acs.text: Each package card lists that package's features.

expected_answer.operand: package card lists that package's features

judgements.rationale: Applied money because the feature publishes fixed paid-package prices and package-selection controls; applied user-reach because every author comparing packages encounters these rules; applied change-frequency because package content, availability text, and seat fixtures are likely to change across releases. Did not apply auth because the source states there is no sign-in, and did not apply data-loss because this use-case is read-only package comparison.
